question.problem:
The disjoint union ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔{A}_{3}$ of events ${A}_{1},{A}_{2},{A}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space. Compute $P({A}_{3}|B)$ given the following probabilities:

$$
\begin{aligned} & P(B|{A}_{1})=0.5, &  \\  & P(B|{A}_{2})=0.6, & P({A}_{2})=0.2 \\  & P(B|{A}_{3})=0.1, & P({A}_{3})=0.7\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If the disjoint union ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔…⊔{A}_{n}$ covers the entire sample space, Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability gives us the following:

$$
P({A}_{k}|B)=\frac{P(B|{A}_{k})P({A}_{k})}{P(B)}=\frac{P(B|{A}_{k})P({A}_{k})}{{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}P(B|{A}_{i})P({A}_{i})}
$$

where $k=1,2,…,n.$

In our case, $n=3,$ and ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔{A}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space. Consequently, we have

$$
P({A}_{1})+P({A}_{2})+P({A}_{3})=1.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}_{1}) & =1-(P({A}_{2})+P({A}_{3})) \\  & =1-(0.2+0.7) \\  & =0.1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}_{3}|B) & =\frac{P(B|{A}_{3})P({A}_{3})}{{\sum }_{i=1}^{3}P(B|{A}_{i})P({A}_{i})} \\  & =\frac{P(B|{A}_{3})P({A}_{3})}{P(B|{A}_{1})P({A}_{1})+P(B|{A}_{2})P({A}_{2})+P(B|{A}_{3})P({A}_{3})} \\  & =\frac{(0.1)(0.7)}{(0.5)(0.1)+(0.6)(0.2)+(0.1)(0.7)} \\  & =\frac{0.07}{0.24} \\  & ≈0.29.\end{aligned}
$$
